human_tolerance.notes: Comfortable in wooded gardens, hedgerows and near buildings, where it works along the ground and in low shrubs and carries food away in its cheek pouches.

phases.name: caching
phases.note: Fills its burrow with stored food ahead of winter.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: During the winter the chipmunk may enter long periods of hibernation, though it is not an obligate hibernator and the strategy stays ActiveYearRound.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: Moult occurs once or twice annually, during May or June and sometimes again in October.

vocalizations.description: A high, rapid trill, measured at about 130 trills per minute, given while moving along the ground and from a burrow entrance.
A sharp, single chip given when it is startled or when a predator is near its burrow.

range.note: Native to eastern North America, from the Gulf Coast north into eastern Canada.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walks and runs on the ground and climbs; its Ojibwe name is said to translate as 'one who descends trees headlong'.

traits.nest_type.note: Lives in and defends a burrow, lined with leaves, rocks, sticks and other material.

traits.perching.note: A ground-and-climbing rodent; it does not perch like a bird.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 111.91 g and PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 93.40 g; both fall inside Wikipedia's stated 66-150 g range.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia gives about 30 cm in length including the tail, consistent with PanTHERIA's AdultHeadBodyLen_mm of 146.47 plus a bushy tail.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia states that eastern chipmunks live three or more years on average in the wild, and up to eight years in captivity.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Seed 30 mapped to 'seed', Diet-Fruit 20 to 'fruit', Diet-PlantO 30 to 'browse' (bulbs and green plants), Diet-Inv 20 to 'invertebrate'. Wikipedia lists bulbs, seeds, fruits, nuts, green plants, mushrooms, insects, worms and bird eggs, and notes it carries food in its cheek pouches.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia states that it defends its burrow and lives a solitary life except during mating season and while the young are with the mother, roughly six to eight weeks after birth.

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Activity-Diurnal 1 (Nocturnal 0, Crepuscular 0); Wikipedia describes daytime activity with winter dormancy.

traits.defense.note: Retreats to its burrow and darts away from a threat; judgement mapping to the schema's single-value field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: it works close to cover with a burrow within easy reach, so it is moderately wary but readily habituated where people leave food out.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value is 'G' (ground). An arboreal share is retained because Wikipedia describes the animal climbing trees and descending them headlong, and moving between ground and canopy; the split is judgement.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the burrow, leaf-litter and cavity weights are judgement, since no open source gives their relative use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement: the eastern chipmunk is common in wooded gardens, hedgerows and around buildings across its range and is a familiar sight for people living in eastern North America; no allow-listed open source quantifies its tolerance of built land.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia states the chipmunk 'may enter long periods of hibernation' during winter, which is not an obligate dormancy, so ActiveYearRound is used with a dormancy phase.

seasonal.phases.note: Winter hibernation, the May-June and sometimes October moults, and the cheek-pouch food transport are from Wikipedia; the caching window and the calendar boundaries are authored judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Females usually produce one or two litters of three to five young, and the young stay with the mother for about six to eight weeks, giving the 56-day juvenile window; the 0.6 scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.trill.note: Wikipedia records a trill measured at about 130 trills per minute; the day window and cooldown are authored judgement. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.alarm_chip.note: No allow-listed open source describes this species' alarm call; the wording and cooldown here are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description: reddish-brown fur above with five dark brown stripes along the back contrasting with light brown stripes, a dark tail, a tawny stripe running from the whiskers to below the ears and light stripes over the eyes. The proportions and the stripes and bushy-tail boxes are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program, scaled down for a 100 g rodent: it flees 8 m at a trot, forages on the walk for seed, and rests while the sun is below the horizon. The climb mode has no pose in the body plan, so no climb pose is declared.
